scene.speaker: nova
scene.bubble: Look how far we've come! Learn the present perfect passive to say what has been achieved this year.
scene.intro: Our Inspiring Nordic — Trades project has reached an exciting point. In this unit you read about everything that has been achieved by Grade 9 this year, you learn the present perfect passive to report finished results, and you talk about what has been done in your own life. When a job is complete and we want the result, we say 'It has been done.' Let's practise it.

activities.title: Vocabulary — projects and results. Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.right: something good and difficult that you have succeeded in doing
the latest time by which something must be finished
the amount of money you have to spend on something
an event where you show your work to the public
an important stage or moment in a project
money or things given to help a person or project

activities.title: Reading — what the class has achieved

data.title: A year of Trades: what has already been done
data.author: nadia
data.text:
It is hard to believe how much has been achieved this year in our Inspiring Nordic — Trades project. Twelve months ago the workshop was tired and empty. Today it is one of the busiest rooms in school.

Since September, the old benches have been repaired and new tools have been bought with a careful budget. A small garden has been planted behind the building, and the safety rules have been printed on bright new posters.

Money has mattered too. A generous donation has been given by a local carpenter, and every coin has been recorded by the treasurer. Because of this, our deadline has been met without stress.

Mateo is proud of the teamwork. “Nothing here has been done by one person,” he says. Liam agrees: “Every job has been shared, so every success belongs to all of us.”

The biggest milestone is still to come. A public exhibition has been organised for December, when families will see exactly what has been built, mended and imagined by Grade 9.

data.title: Present perfect passive
data.intro: We use the present perfect passive to report a finished action when we care about the result, not who did it. It is perfect for project reports about what is already complete.

examples.text: The plan has been approved by the head.
Many hours have been spent on this.

rules: Form: has/have + been + past participle (The room has been cleaned).
Use it for a finished action with a result we can see now.
Add by + person only if the doer is important.

items.sentence: The old workshop ___ been renovated completely.
New tools ___ been bought with our budget.
A garden has been ___ behind the building.
The safety posters have ___ printed already.
Our deadline ___ been met without stress.

activities.title: Open cloze — complete the results report. Write ONE word in each gap.

data.text: This year a lot {1} been achieved by Grade 9. The old workshop has {2} renovated completely. New tools {3} been bought with our budget. A garden has been {4} in the yard. Two exhibitions {5} been organised so far. We are proud of everything that has been {6}.

activities.title: Listening — the head teacher's message. Write ONE word in each gap.

data.voice_note: Voz: la profesora (Miss Vega), celebrando los resultados del proyecto.
data.script: Hello, Grade 9. I want to celebrate what has been done this year for Inspiring Nordic. The workshop has been renovated, and it looks wonderful. Many new tools have been bought with our budget. A small garden has been planted behind the building. The final exhibition has been planned for December. Nadia has been chosen to present our results to the parents. Every task has been completed on time. I am very proud of you. Well done, everyone, and keep going!

activities.title: Speaking — what has been done. In pairs, then record it.

data.text: In pairs, talk about results using the present perfect passive. Model: “What has been done in your classroom this year?” — “The walls have been painted and new books have been added.” 1) What has been improved in your school recently? 2) What has been organised for your class this term? 3) In the Trades project, what has already been built or repaired? 4) What good thing has been achieved by your team? Then record your best answers.

homework.prompt: Write a short report (6–8 sentences) about what has been done in your school or in the Trades project this year. Use the present perfect passive at least four times, for example: 'The workshop has been renovated' and 'New tools have been bought'. Capital letters and full stops!
